recipes.name: Creamy Banana Pudding
ingredients_raw: 1 (3.4 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix

steps.text: Stir condensed milk and water together in a medium bowl; beat in pudding mix until smooth. Chill mixture in the refrigerator for 5 minutes.
Whip cream in a separate bowl until stiff peaks form. Fold whipped cream into chilled pudding mixture.
Dip sliced bananas in lemon juice. Shake off excess.
Spoon 1 cup of the pudding mixture into a 2 ½ quart serving bowl. Top with 1/3 each of the wafers, bananas, and remaining pudding. Repeat layers twice. Chill until serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamy Banana Pudding
raw_recipe.description: No-cook creamy banana pudding made with heavy cream, instant vanilla pudding, and condensed milk — and, of course, bananas and vanilla wafer cookies!

review.reviewBody: HELPFUL TIPS NOT MENTIONED: My extremely picky never satisfied husband loved this as well as my toddlers, so what more could I want! I wanted to note for those making this for the 1st time that this calls for heavy cream aka heavy whipping cream which is not whipping cream (cool whip) in the freezer section. I believe THIS is why people complain about this being too sweet b/c quite frankly I CHOSE THIS RECIPE because it was the least sweetest of ALL the recipes on here which I DID try. Heavy Whipping Cream doesn't have that nice sugary taste as the frozen whipped creams you put on top of desserts nor is it something people can eat right out of the carton w/o adding something else. Outside of that, I just eyeball the amount of nilla wafers or Pepperidge Farm Chessmen cookies (try it!), and set it in the fridge for a few hours (necessary) to allow them to soften up. THIS ALSO allows the lemon taste of bananas to go away! It also helps delay browning. 3 THINLY sliced Bananas with 1/4C lemon (used my measuring cup to place juice&dunked the slices as I put it on the layer) was the perfect amount w/o letting anything go to waste. I chose this recipe b/c unlike others, I didn't have to wait for my cream cheese & frozen whipped cream to soften at room temp. UPDATE: To cut down even more on the sweetness, this works better with just ONE CUP of heavy whipped cream. Tastes more like pudding instead of "whipped" and I use fat-free condensed milk

This is excellent! The recipe is rich and yields many more than 6-8 servings. I’d say 12-16 servings is more like it. I made the Gaines’ Aunt Opal’s recipe that includes cream cheese and the Gaines’ Magnolias recipe that does not include cream cheese. In a side by side comparison, the one without cream cheese is better according to myself (a cream cheese lover) and my grandchildren (not cream cheese lovers). The cream cheese lends a denser texture which almost feels a bit greasy whereas the one without it was lighter and more pleasant. (I can’t believe I’m saying that given my preference for all things cream cheese!) The flavors are much better when given time to blend so making this a day ahead is definitely the way to go. Also, there is not any major improvement in flavor after approx. 24 hours of wait time. I was tempted to use banana cream pudding rather than vanilla because I wasn’t sure there would be enough banana flavor however, in the end I was glad I used the vanilla since the banana flavor is wonderful (again, you need to let it sit 24 hours to let the banana flavor permeate this dessert). In regards to the bananas, buy them green. I used 2 very large bananas in the cream cheese recipe and 3 very large bananas in the one without cream cheese. We all preferred the one with more banana. I sliced the bananas about 1/4” (+/-) thick on my large cutting board, spread them out and gave them a light brushing of lemon juice. Then I flipped the banana slices over and applied another thin layer of lemon juice. I had no problems with the bananas tasting too lemony nor browning even after a couple days. Surprisingly, all but one of us preferred it with the Great Value brand of Nilla Wafers since they were more cakey than the brand name. We topped it with a 1” layer of homemade whipped cream and sprinkled that with the wafer crumbs left in the bottom of the bag. Lastly, because the yield was so high, I ended up freezing it. I was pleased the flavor was still good however, certainly not as good as when it was freshly made.

Made this when I happened to have extra bananas, and nilla wafers. I ommitted the sweet condensed milk and the heavy cream since I just didn't have it. Instead I made a package of instant vanilla pudding, added some vanilla yogurt and mixed it. I added some cinnamon to this mixture to give it more flavor. I soaked my bananas in a water/lime juice mixture. Then I layered the nilla cookies, bananas, and the pudding/yogurt mixtures. Delish and healthy as a dessert can be ;).

This is Magnolia Bakery 's famous banana pudding recipe. The condensed milk/ water / pudding mix needs to chill for at least an hour. Should be 3 hours or even overnight. The pudding will not set properly otherwise. That's why so many people are saying it's just watery

This made a lot of dessert. My box of pudding was banana flavor and it was 5 oz. so I used it all and added a little whole milk to make up for the difference. I only had 2 bananas. This is really good and it made a very filled bowl. Overall this was way too sweet for me, so a small portion goes a long way. I did not dip my bananas in lemon juice as they were covered in pudding and weren't going to turn brown. My husband said, "that stuff's dangerous" after eating a bowl. It's good. The only thing I would do differently is make this enough ahead so the cookies will soften. I made this two hours ahead, but it wasn't enough time and they were still a little crunchy. It didn't slow any of us down from eating it, but I've prefer the softer cookie that melds more with the pudding. While the banana pudding worked, the vanilla might have been a bit less rich. I prefer whole milk as this was too sweet for me, but no one mentioned it.

This pudding turned out great, very light and creamy. I took another person's suggestion to use only half the condensed milk and use regular milk for the other half. It turned out to have the perfect amount of sweetness, I couldn't imagine it with the full amount of sweetened milk. Also, like others, I filled a small bowl with citrus soda and sliced the bananas right into the bowl and then drained them. I let the pudding sit in the fridge for about 10 hours before eating. Can't wait to make it again on a hot summer day.

Very good recipe! A bit on the sweet side, so next time I will use less than the called amount of the condensed milk. I also used a pint of heavy whipping cream for the entire recipe, I used 1 and 1/2 cup for the pudding and the rest of the pint for some unsweetened whipped topping. I also added about a teaspoon of pure vanilla extract to give it a bit more vanilla flavor. I did not have any lemon flavor on my bananas either, I sliced them and poured some (not much at all) lemom juice over them and mixed them up so I didnt waste any juice. And I let it sit in the fridge overnight. Overall very good recipe. I would also like to try this recipe with homemade pudding instead of instant!!! :-)

I've made this for years but instead of vanilla wafers, I layer with graham crackers and people LOSE THEIR MINDS when I make it! lol ALWAYS let it sit in the fridge overnight and never use Cool Whip or anything like that as a substitute for the heavy whipping cream. It makes all the difference!...and FRENCH vanilla pudding mix : )

I made a gluten free version of this. The only change was I used Glutino's Vanilla Creme cookies instead of vanilla wafers. I also used French Vanilla pudding mix instead of regular Vanilla. Everyone, all ages, loved it. So easy!!
This recipe was wonderful and so easy. My family loves it-I have to make it for all of the family get-togethers. For more banana flavor I substitute banana cream instant pudding for the vanilla.

This is the easiest and best tasting banana pudding! For a fun variation, I omit the vanilla wafters and use chocolate graham crackers and make "sandwiches" with peanut butter. I break them into squares to layer into dish and follow everything else in recipe. The chocolate and peanut butter go great with the bananas!
My family absolutely went crazy over this!
good very sweet, be sure to use INSTANT pudding, I almost made this mistake.
This is easy to make and my entire family is begging me to make it again. Thanks for this one!
I make this amazing banana pudding for every Christmas. It has become such a tradition that the first thing my family asks is if I brought banana pudding!
I've loved this recipe and have never had any complaints. But this time my pudding mixture will not set up in the fridge. I don't know what I did wrong. I am open to suggestions.

Terrible recipe! Pretty sure something is missing from the steps or was miswritten as I followed all the steps to the tee and it came out nothing close to pudding. I ended up with a big bowl of liquid and a big waste of time!
